newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-ROMANIA WANT IORDANESCU TO CONCENTRATE ON NATIONAL SIDE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMANIA WANT IORDANESCU TO CONCENTRATE ON NATIONAL SIDE.

text.p: The Romanian Soccer Federation (FRF) has rejected national team trainer Anghel Iordanescu's request to let him coach both the Romanian national squad and Greek first division AEK Athens at the same time.
"Iordanescu's contract with us runs until December 1997. He must train Romania's national team until the deal expires," FRF spokesman Cristian Bivolaru said on Friday.
"Iordanescu cannot coach AEK Athens too. That would prevent him from fulfilling his duties to the Romanian national team and it would also breach his contract."
Earlier this month Iordanescu asked the FRF to allow him to coach both sides. Greek sports media said he had been offered a contract worth $1.0 million a year by the Athens club.

Iordanescu, 46, became Romania's trainer in 1993 and took the side to the World Cup quarter-finals in 1994. Romania lead their current preliminary group and are virtually sure of qualifying for the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
